projects.title: The House of Karji
projects.overview:
Karji is a growing multi-brand retailer of luxury fragrances, watches, accessories and gift sets in the UAE. The catalogue needed cleaner collections, proper brand pages, multi-channel product feeds and a full redesign from Figma.
I rebuilt the storefront mobile-first from the Figma design — motion, auto-sliding carousels, product-card hover effects and smooth page transitions — and moved brands, collections and merchandising rules into data the team edits from the Shopify theme editor.
projects.features:
Full Figma-to-Shopify redesign with motion, carousels and page transitions
Mega menu with nested SEO-friendly URLs and editor-managed images
Brand pages driven by a Shopify metaobject: logo, banner or video, meta title and description
Smart collections: hidden out-of-stock items, auto New Arrivals and a 30-day “New” label
Gift-with-purchase samples added to the cart by brand and gender rules
Sticky gallery product page with Tabby/Tamara “Split into 4” and WhatsApp contact
Mobile toolbar, glassmorphism Filter & Sort bar and accordion footer
Multi-channel XML feed for Google, Meta and TikTok; free shipping above AED 200
projects.journey: Shoppers enter through the mega menu or a brand page, filter with the floating Filter & Sort bar and land on a sticky-gallery product page with instalment options. Free fragrance samples matching the brand and gender of their cart are added automatically and grouped into one “Free samples” strip.
projects.engineering: Brand pages are a single template fed by a metaobject, so a new brand is a content entry, not a code change. Collection rules hide out-of-stock items and keep Watches pure; the Instagram section uses pasted post links and uploaded media instead of heavy embeds. A Safari CSS Grid bug and the Order Printer invoice were fixed along the way.
projects.scope: Figma redesign, theme development, merchandising logic, product feeds, shipping rules, blog consolidation with article SEO metafields and a three-layout policy section with a scrollspy table of contents — all built on a duplicate theme and previewed before publishing.
projects.approach: A redesign like this starts with the catalogue model — brands, collections and merchandising rules — before any pixels move.
projects.steps:
Audit catalogue, collections and URLs
Model brands and rules as metaobjects
Build sections from Figma on a duplicate theme
Wire feeds, tracking and shipping
Preview, QA on Safari and mobile, publish

projects.title: Atelier Perfumery
projects.overview:
Atelier Perfumery sells around 1,500 products from more than 130 designer and niche fragrance brands. The store had slow hero loading, misaligned product grids, placeholder product content and no proper tracking or feeds.
I fixed performance and product content on the live theme, added full-funnel GA4 tracking and a reusable Google Merchant Center feed, and am rebuilding the store from Figma as a hand-built theme.
projects.features:
Hero banner loads first; smoother carousels and single-line titles to stop card misalignment
A–Z brand directory with 132 logos served from the Shopify CDN
Product pages with real descriptions and auto-generated notes from Top / Middle / Base
Fragrance Palette with pyramid note icons
Wallet buttons and a cart discount field matched to the theme
GA4 dataLayer via GTM plus a Shopify Custom Pixel for checkout and purchase
Reusable Google Merchant Center XML feed (RSS 2.0 + g: namespace)
New Figma theme: in-place category switching, glass sticky Add to Cart, Tabby + Tamara card
projects.journey: Customers browse by category without page reloads — each view keeps a shareable ?category= URL — then use the floating Filter & Sort pill, open a product with its fragrance pyramid, and buy from a glassmorphic sticky Add to Cart bar with instalment options in one card.
projects.engineering: Tracking runs in two layers: a storefront dataLayer through Google Tag Manager, and a Shopify Custom Pixel for begin_checkout, add_shipping_info, add_payment_info and purchase. The Merchant Center feed is a single template that works on any Shopify store by changing one config block.
projects.scope: Performance fixes, brand directory, product-page rebuild, payments styling, analytics, feeds and an in-progress full Figma rebuild on a preview theme.
projects.approach: Large catalogues reward fixing the data model first: real product content and consistent brand assets make every later design change cheaper.
projects.steps:
Measure loading order and layout shift
Replace placeholder product content
Ship tracking and feeds
Rebuild from Figma on a preview theme
QA and publish

projects.title: Flower District
projects.overview:
Flower District sells luxury bouquets and bespoke event flowers with same-day and next-day delivery across seven emirates, plus physical stores that need local search traffic.
I set up emirate-based delivery pricing, date and time-slot delivery, a cart-only checkout flow and standalone store landing pages built for Google Business Profile and “near me” Google Ads.

Emirate-based delivery pricing through Shopify shipping rates (AED 35 / AED 80, free above AED 250)
Date and time-slot delivery with the Kite app and delivery estimates in the cart
Add-ons such as message cards and balloons
Cart-only checkout flow with WhatsApp-only order updates
Mobile hamburger navigation with collection categories
Store landing pages with map, hours, call/WhatsApp and directions
Wallet button alignment and a GA4 dataLayer across the full funnel

Order updates arrive on WhatsApp. Local shoppers find the nearest store through Google and land on a page with map, hours and one-tap directions.

projects.title: Daima
projects.overview:
Daima’s product page had a misaligned Google Pay button and product blocks rendering outside the product form.
I traced it to an invalid nested <form> in the theme’s add-to-cart block, rebuilt the block so the page has exactly one product form, and then aligned payments and BNPL widgets inside it. I also handled the blog migration, theme maintenance and a coming-soon page for Daima’s US branch.
projects.features:
Root-cause fix for an invalid nested product form
Buy with Google Pay matched to Add to Cart width, height, radius and font
Tabby and Tamara blocks placed correctly inside the product form
Blog migration and theme maintenance
Coming-soon landing page for daimadubai.com (US branch)
projects.journey: Shoppers now see one consistent buy box — Add to Cart, Google Pay and instalment options aligned — instead of blocks breaking out of the layout.
projects.engineering: Browsers silently drop nested forms, so the theme’s markup produced a different DOM from the one the CSS expected. Fixing the markup, not adding CSS overrides, removed the whole class of layout bugs.
projects.scope: Theme bug fix, payment button styling, BNPL placement, blog migration and a separate coming-soon page.
projects.approach: When a layout breaks unpredictably, validate the HTML before writing CSS.
projects.steps:
Reproduce on mobile and desktop
Validate the product form markup
Rebuild the block
Re-style payment buttons
Regression test and publish

projects.title: Juvenis Paris
projects.overview:
Juvenis Paris needed sharper mobile presentation, instalment widgets under the buy buttons and a mobile swipe interaction that did not need two swipes to move.
I added separate mobile banners, placed Tabby and Tamara under the buy buttons, rewrote the swipe interaction with 1:1 finger tracking and momentum, and built a premium editorial maintenance page on cPanel.
projects.features:
Separate mobile banner images with focal point and responsive <picture> markup
Tabby and Tamara widgets directly under the buy buttons
“Below title” price position setting added to the section schema
Rewritten mobile swipe: 1:1 tracking, momentum, axis-locking, no double swipe
Validated with a 13-scenario automated swipe test
Editorial maintenance page in ivory, mocha and gold (Fraunces + Jost)
projects.journey: On mobile, collection banners are art-directed for the phone, product swipes follow the finger exactly, and instalment options sit right below the buy buttons.
projects.engineering: The swipe rewrite separates gesture tracking from animation: the gesture follows the finger, axis-locks to avoid fighting vertical scroll, then hands off to GSAP for momentum. An automated 13-scenario test guards the behaviour.
projects.scope: Theme customisation, BNPL widgets, mobile interaction rewrite and a static maintenance site.
projects.approach: Mobile gestures need tests, not eyeballing: script the swipes you care about.
projects.steps:

Automate the scenarios

projects.title: DREC Property Management System
projects.overview:
The system manages the full hierarchy from landlord to internal tenant company, property and plot, unit or warehouse, subtenant and EJARI registration. Property managers track main leases and subleases, finance users follow invoices and receipts, and the dashboard summarises occupancy, contract value and upcoming expiries.

Built with Next.js 16, TypeScript, Prisma, Zustand and Recharts, with role-based access for super administrators, property managers, finance users and read-only viewers. The data model was designed from the client's lease spreadsheet. All company names, contract numbers, plot numbers and amounts in the mockups were replaced with fictional demonstration values.

A manager opens the dashboard, sees occupancy and leases approaching expiry, then drills into a property, its units and the subleases attached to them. Compliance alerts point to contracts, EJARI registrations or licences that need action, and reports export the data for review.

Each level of the hierarchy is a related record, so totals on the dashboard come from the same data the registers display. Expiry checks generate compliance alerts, and an audit log records changes. Role checks limit editing to the appropriate users.

Developed application for a property management client. Data import from the client's spreadsheets is part of the build; publication of client-identifying details requires the client's approval.
projects.features:
Companies, properties, plots and unit registers
Main lease and sublease contracts with fee calculations
Subtenant records with trade licence tracking
EJARI registration status and expiry tracking
Rent collection with invoices and receipts
Compliance alerts, reports and role-based access
projects.journey: A manager opens the dashboard, sees occupancy and leases approaching expiry, then drills into a property, its units and the subleases attached to them. Compliance alerts point to contracts, EJARI registrations or licences that need action, and reports export the data for review.
projects.engineering: Each level of the hierarchy is a related record, so totals on the dashboard come from the same data the registers display. Expiry checks generate compliance alerts, and an audit log records changes. Role checks limit editing to the appropriate users.
projects.scope: Developed application for a property management client. Data import from the client's spreadsheets is part of the build; publication of client-identifying details requires the client's approval.
projects.approach: This project shows how a lease spreadsheet can become a structured operational system. A similar platform starts with the ownership hierarchy, contract types, renewal rules and the regulatory registrations the team must track.
projects.steps:
Model the portfolio from landlord and company down to units and subtenants.
Record leases and subleases with values, dates and EJARI references.
Track rent invoices, receipts and outstanding balances.
Surface expiries and compliance actions before they become problems.

Dropdown navigation for Perfume, Oud Tradition, Home Fragrance and Body Scent
Menus built through the Shopify Admin GraphQL API
Canonical collection URLs instead of tag filters
Ongoing store management, feeds and campaign support

projects.title: Mino Suppliers
projects.overview:
Mino Suppliers combines a marketing website with a trade portal. Visitors browse sustainable tissue, towel and napkin products and apply for a wholesale account. Approved business customers sign in to order at their own pricing tier, reuse order guides, route large orders for approval and follow invoices on net terms.

Built with Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL. Pricing tiers and customer-specific prices are resolved on the server, and orders above a company's approval threshold wait for an approver. The mockups use fictional customers and demonstration orders.

A prospective customer reads about the products, submits a wholesale enquiry and is approved by the team. Purchasers then order from the portal at their agreed prices, approvers review orders above the limit, and finance follows invoices — while admins see leads, customers, orders and revenue in one place.

Roles distinguish visitors, purchasers, approvers, company owners and staff. Prices, approval rules and payment terms come from the customer's company record, so the same catalogue shows the correct commercial terms for each account.

Developed application. Card payment, email notifications and analytics are designed as later integrations; the documented scope covers the website, portal and administration.

Product catalogue with certifications and recycled content
Wholesale application and lead management
Customer-specific pricing tiers and discounts
Order guides, cart and net-terms checkout

projects.title: Mechaura International
projects.overview:
Mechaura International is an industrial supplier website organised around products, sectors and quotation enquiries. Its catalogue covers abrasive brushes, bearings, hydraulic hoses and pumps, filtration, cutting tools and elevator accessories. Product imagery and motion content help buyers understand the range before contacting the supplier.

The project uses a Vite build with generated product, sector, location and article pages, a sitemap and llms.txt workflow and optimised image assets. A companion WordPress theme packages the same design for WordPress hosting. The device mockups are captured from the production build of the website.

Buyers can enter through search, a product category, an industry or a city page, review relevant equipment and move to a quotation enquiry. The website separates product information from company and service content so technical and commercial visitors can find an appropriate next step.

projects.title: Finora
projects.overview:
Finora is a business accounting application designed around the daily work of UAE trading and service companies. Sales, purchases, expenses and inventory connect to a double-entry ledger. Teams can review invoices, payments, bank transactions and reports within the same organisation workspace.

The implementation uses Next.js, TypeScript and Prisma, with money stored in integer minor units. The source includes balanced journal posting, reversing entries, document numbering, inventory movements, UAE VAT handling and role-based access. The device mockups were captured from a local build running demonstration data for a fictional trading company; no customer or financial records are shown.

Users move from a customer or supplier record to a commercial document, then to posting and settlement. Every invoice shows the journal entries it created, so staff can trace a balance back to its source. The dashboard summarises cash, receivables and payables and links overdue items to the underlying records.

Financial documents feed balanced journal entries rather than isolated dashboard totals. The code represents amounts in fils and handles corrections through reversing entries. Tenant context, roles and server-side validation are part of the implementation, alongside reporting, approvals and recurring documents.

Deployed on Railway — open the live demo from this page. The documented scope includes accounting, inventory, banking, reports and account administration. The assistant and external services depend on their configured providers. Tax settings and financial reports need business-specific review before operational use; the portfolio does not represent regulatory certification.

projects.title: CertGuard
projects.overview:
CertGuard centralises domains, SSL/TLS certificates, servers and DNS providers for teams that manage many websites. Instead of trusting manually entered dates, it checks domain registration data and inspects the certificate served by each site, then flags mismatches, upcoming expiries and errors.

The application uses Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL. Domain expiry comes from RDAP, certificates are inspected over a live TLS connection, and issuance follows an ACME workflow with HTTP-01 or DNS-01 validation. The mockups use the built-in demonstration data (example.com-style domains).

An administrator adds a domain; CertGuard verifies registration and certificate details and marks the record as verified or mismatched. The dashboard and notifications highlight what expires soon, and renewals can be requested, installed and verified with every step recorded.

Verification, issuance and installation are separate services behind interfaces, so providers can be swapped. Credentials and tokens are stored encrypted, deployments validate configuration before reload and roll back on failure, and every operation writes an audit entry.

Developed application. Live certificate issuance and installation require configured ACME, DNS and SSH access; without them the issuance pipeline runs in a clearly marked simulation mode.

RDAP domain verification and live SSL inspection
Stored-versus-discovered date comparison
ACME certificate request, renewal and rollback
SSH server registry with Nginx and Apache operations
Email, WhatsApp, Telegram and Slack alerts
Automation logs, reports and role-based access

projects.title: WorkFlow Hub
projects.overview:
WorkFlow Hub is built around a common operations loop: a request arrives by email, someone reads it, assigns it, replies and follows up until it is done. It covers website, online payments, web development, store support and back-office categories. Each task has a single owner, a due date and an activity history.

The application uses Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL with session-based sign-in for administrators and employees. An AI step extracts the subject, sender, summary, category and priority from a pasted email and drafts an editable reply. The device mockups were captured from a local build running demonstration data; names, branches and tasks are fictional.

An administrator pastes an email, reviews the extracted details and the suggested reply, then creates the task and assigns an employee. The assignee is notified, updates status on the board and adds comments. The follow-up engine reminds owners before due dates and flags work that stalls.

Scheduled jobs evaluate due dates, review reminders and renewal windows against configurable thresholds. Status changes write activity logs and notifications. Role checks separate administrator screens such as employees, settings and reports from the employee workspace.

Developed internal application. Outlook mailbox integration and AI drafting depend on configured providers; drafts are always reviewed before a reply is sent from the user's own mail client.

projects.title: Koshys Nursing Study
projects.category: AI study platform for nursing students
projects.overview:
A study platform for Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing students at Koshys College of Nursing, Bangalore.
It generates source-grounded, exam-ready answers with diagrams and flashcards, analyses previous-year question papers by subject, offers an AI tutor and tracks each student’s clinical record checklist — with no account needed.
projects.features:
Study generator with diagrams and flashcards
Ask-the-tutor AI assistant
Previous-year question papers by subject
Clinical records checklist with progress
Local-only storage with data backup
projects.journey: A student picks a topic such as congestive heart failure, gets a structured exam answer with a diagram and flashcards, then practises with past papers.
projects.engineering: Answers are grounded in course sources, and all notes and progress stay in the student’s browser, so the site needs no accounts or personal data.
projects.scope: Education web application deployed on Railway.
projects.approach: Study tools should start from the real syllabus and past papers, not generic AI output.
projects.steps:
Collect syllabus and papers
Ground the generator
Design study views
Ship without accounts
